originality.rationale: Craizer–Teixeira–da Silva 2012 full Springer research text concerns equal-area deterministic convex n-gons approximating affine arclength, not the probability that 3 independent points yield tiny Euclidean area nor a sampling-density variational problem. Henze 1983 samples 3 points uniformly from the interior of a convex K (measure zero on the boundary), and the classical circular inscribed-triangle model does not dominate the arbitrary strictly convex curve and optimizing f. Resultary searches for small-area random boundary triangles and affine arclength found no earlier matching general coefficient. The beta cusp integral and optimal density are presented as new applications, not a claim that affine arclength itself was discovered here.
